subject: Support economics & escalation coverage — structured offer and crediting
content:
--- Message 1 ---
From: Elena Rojas <elena@brightlane.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightlane.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring SLA options for Brightlane pilot (uptime + escalation)

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and cost controls. Before we move internal approvals, procurement asked for a clear breakdown on support economics: uptime tiers, guaranteed response times for sev1/2, and how escalation coverage looks across on-call and weekend support.

Attached is a short form with the scenarios we'd like priced (30 / 99.95 / 99.99 uptime bands, 1-hour/4-hour response windows, and 24x7 vs. business-hours escalation). We also want to understand any volume or term discounts, and whether uptime credits are capped (and how they're calculated).

Can you send a packaged offer that shows (a) cost delta between tiers, (b) how credits scale, and (c) what an accelerated on-call retainer looks like for the first 12 months? If possible, we'd like a trial period with a limited credit escrow.

Best,
Elena
Director of Cloud Ops, Brightlane Systems
[Attachment: Brightlane_SLA_Request_Form.pdf (PDF, 134KB)]

--- Message 2 ---
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@brightlane.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring SLA options for Brightlane pilot (uptime + escalation)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attached form. I've looped in Grace (Sales Ops) and Marcus (SRE pricing) to make sure we model the economics correctly. High level answers below; I'll include a short package PDF and an XLS with the tier math by EOD.

Quick summary:
- Uptime bands: 99.9 (standard), 99.95 (enhanced), 99.99 (premium). Pricing delta is primarily driven by reserve capacity & regional failover planning.
- Response windows: Sev1 (1 hour) and Sev2 (4 hours) are available in Enhanced/Premium; standard includes 4-hour business-hours for Sev1 and 8-hour for Sev2.
- Escalation coverage: 24x7 for Premium; business-hours + 24x7 on-call retainer for Enhanced.
- Credits: Calculated pro-rata on monthly committed spend; caps at 100% of monthly fee for the affected month. For pilot programs we can offer an escrowed trial credit pool (one-time, non-recurring) of up to 10% of first-quarter committed spend.

Open questions for us to price precisely:
1) Expected committed monthly throughput (tokens/day or GPU hours)
2) Preferred term (12 / 24 / 36 months) — longer terms unlock step discounts and larger credit pools
3) Whether Brightlane requires on-prem/private control plane (affects operational cost)

I'll attach a structured workbook showing a few scenarios (low/medium/high commit) plus an optional accelerated on-call retainer SKU that buys 24x7 pager routing and guaranteed 30-minute escalation to an incident commander.

Thanks — we'll follow up with a formal quote and a redline-friendly SOW.

- Nikhil
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 ---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@brightlane.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 11:55:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring SLA options for Brightlane pilot (uptime + escalation)

Hi Elena —

Attaching the workbook and a short support-tier one-pager. A few clarifications inline:

- Attachment: Redwood_Support_Tiers_v2.xlsx (see tabs: Scenario_Summary, Credit_Calculation, Retainer_SKUs)

Key assumptions used in the scenarios:
• Pilot commit: 500k tokens/day ~ estimated 120 GPU hours/day (us-west region)
• Term: 12 months (pilot + potential roll)
• Failover plan: regional warm standby for 99.95; active-active for 99.99

Example outputs from the workbook (monthly):
• 99.9 (standard): $12k support + no retainer; credits for missed uptime <= 50% of monthly support fee
• 99.95 (enhanced): $28k support + optional 24x7 retainer $18k/month; credits pro-rata, capped at 100% of monthly support fee; on-call retainer includes 30-min escalation SLA
• 99.99 (premium): $55k support + mandatory 24x7 retainer $30k/month; credits formula includes service-level multipliers for multi-region failover

Trial escrow option: for a signed 12-month pilot we can set aside a one-time trial credit pool equal to 10% of the first quarter's committed support fee. Credits draw from the pool first, then standard monthly crediting applies. This is revocable for misuse but otherwise applies against invoices.

Regarding discounts: volume step discounts are applied to the support fee (not token usage) at thresholds of 2x/5x committed throughput. We can also consider an early-payment 2% net-15 concession.

Marcus, two questions for you to confirm the operational constraints on active-active and warm-standby cost differentials.

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Support_Tiers_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)

--- Message 4 ---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Elena Rojas <elena@brightlane.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring SLA options for Brightlane pilot (uptime + escalation)

Hi all —

Confirmed on the infra notes and a couple of operational caveats to surface for Brightlane:

- Active-active for 99.99 requires regional model variants pinned to avoid cold-start model loads during failover; this increases instance counts by ~1.6x vs single-region (estimates in workbook).
- Warm-standby (99.95) uses a reduced-capacity pool and automated routing; recovery time objective for a regional failover is ~7-12 minutes, but initial tail-latency may spike briefly during cache rebuild.
- The accelerated on-call retainer (30-min escalation) requires a dedicated incident commander rotation for the account during business-critical hours; this is why the retainer price is material.

Operational ask for Brightlane to accept in SOW: permission to run periodic failover drills (announced windows) and a standard incident post-mortem cadence. This allows us to keep credits fair and predictable.

Elena — if you can confirm expected monthly throughput range and preferred term, we can produce a final commercial worksheet and a redline-ready SOW. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd like to go line-by-line.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
